claim: With increased life expectancy, age-associated cognitive decline becomes a growing concern, even in the absence of recognizable neurodegenerative disease.
source: With increased life expectancy, age-associated cognitive decline becomes a growing concern, even in the absence of recognizable neurodegenerative disease.
evidence: This is a statement about the societal context of aging and cognitive decline, drawing on established knowledge about demographic trends and health concerns.

claim: The integrated stress response (ISR) is activated during aging and contributes to age-related brain phenotypes.
source: The integrated stress response (ISR) is activated during aging and contributes to age-related brain phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript showing ISR markers in aged mice.

claim: Treatment with ISRIB reverses ISR activation in the brain, as indicated by decreased levels of ATF4 and phosphorylated eIF2.
source: We demonstrate that treatment with the drug-like small-molecule ISR inhibitor ISRIB reverses ISR activation in the brain, as indicated by decreased levels of activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) and phosphorylated eukaryotic translation initiation factor eIF2.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by Western blot data shown in Figures 1 and 5 demonstrating reduced ATF4 and p-eIF2 levels after ISRIB treatment.

claim: ISRIB treatment reverses spatial memory deficits in old mice.
source: Furthermore, ISRIB treatment reverses spatial memory deficits and ameliorates working memory in old mice.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data from the radial arm water maze shown in Figure 2.

claim: ISRIB treatment ameliorates working memory in old mice.
source: Furthermore, ISRIB treatment reverses spatial memory deficits and ameliorates working memory in old mice.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data from the delayed matching to place paradigm shown in Figure 2C.

claim: ISR inhibition rescues intrinsic neuronal electrophysiological properties in the hippocampus.
source: At the cellular level in the hippocampus, ISR inhibition (i) rescues intrinsic neuronal electrophysiological properties, (ii) restores spine density and (iii) reduces immune profiles, specifically interferon and T cell-mediated responses.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data showing reversal of age-induced AHP increases in Figure 3B.

claim: ISR inhibition restores spine density in the hippocampus.
source: At the cellular level in the hippocampus, ISR inhibition (i) rescues intrinsic neuronal electrophysiological properties, (ii) restores spine density and (iii) reduces immune profiles, specifically interferon and T cell-mediated responses.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data showing increased dendritic spine density in Figure 3E.

claim: ISR inhibition reduces immune profiles, specifically interferon and T cell-mediated responses.
source: At the cellular level in the hippocampus, ISR inhibition (i) rescues intrinsic neuronal electrophysiological properties, (ii) restores spine density and (iii) reduces immune profiles, specifically interferon and T cell-mediated responses.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data showing reduced IFN-related genes (Figure 4A-C) and T cell markers (Figure 4D-E).

claim: Pharmacological interference with the ISR emerges as a promising intervention strategy for combating age-related cognitive decline in otherwise healthy individuals.
source: Thus, pharmacological interference with the ISR emerges as a promising intervention strategy for combating age-related cognitive decline in otherwise healthy individuals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and represents speculation about future therapeutic applications.

claim: Decreases in executive function as well as learning and memory decrements in older, healthy individuals are common.
source: While often discussed in the context of disease, decreases in executive function as well as learning and memory decrements in older, healthy individuals are common (Connelly et al., 1991; Anderson et al., 1998; Kramer et al., 1999; Cepeda et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The aging population is estimated by 2050 to reach 83.7 million individuals above 65 years of age in the US.
source: According to the US Department of Commerce, the aging population is estimated by 2050 to reach 83.7 million individuals above 65 years of age in the US; this represents a rapidly growing healthcare and economic concern (An Aging Nation, 2014).
evidence: This is a demographic projection cited from a government report.

claim: Age-related decline in memory has been recapitulated in preclinical studies with old rodents.
source: Age-related decline in memory has been recapitulated in preclinical studies with old rodents (Chou et al., 2018; Yousef et al., 2019; Villeda et al., 2011; Castellano et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous rodent studies.

claim: Prior studies have identified deficits in spatial memory when comparing young, adult mice with older sex-matched animals.
source: Specifically, prior studies have identified deficits in spatial memory (Villeda et al., 2011; Villeda et al., 2014), working and episodic memory (Yousef et al., 2019; Castellano et al., 2017) and recognition memory (Cabral-Miranda et al., 2020), when comparing young, adult mice with older sex-matched animals.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The hippocampus is the brain region associated with learning and memory formation and is particularly vulnerable to age-related changes in humans and rodents.
source: The hippocampus is the brain region associated with learning and memory formation and is particularly vulnerable to age-related changes in humans and rodents (Disterhoft and Oh, 2007; McKiernan and Marrone, 2017; Oh et al., 2010; Rizzo et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and represents established knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: Deficits in protein synthesis, metabolism, inflammation, and immune responses have been suggested as underlying causes of age-related cognitive decline based on correlative evidence.
source: Deficits in a number of cellular processes have been suggested as underlying causes based on correlative evidence, including protein synthesis (Schimanski and Barnes, 2010), metabolism (Azzu and Valencak, 2017), inflammation (Franceschi et al., 2000), and immune responses (Villeda et al., 2011; Villeda et al., 2014; Baruch et al., 2014; Dulken et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The causal molecular underpinnings of age-related memory decline have remained unclear.
source: While providing a wealth of parameters to assess, by and large the causal molecular underpinnings of age-related memory decline have remained unclear.
evidence: This is an inference based on the state of the field as described in the literature review.

claim: Blocking protein synthesis prevents long-term memory storage.
source: The principle that blocking protein synthesis prevents long-term memory storage was discovered many years ago (Flexner et al., 1962).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a classic study and represents established knowledge.

claim: With age there is a marked decline of protein synthesis in the brain that correlates with defects in proper protein folding.
source: With age there is a marked decline of protein synthesis in the brain that correlates with defects in proper protein folding (Cabral-Miranda et al., 2020; López-Otín et al., 2013; Ingvar et al., 1985; Smith et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Accumulation of misfolded proteins can activate the integrated stress response (ISR).
source: Accumulation of misfolded proteins can activate the integrated stress response (ISR) (Harding et al., 2003), an evolutionary conserved pathway that decreases protein synthesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge about the ISR pathway.

claim: The ISR is an evolutionary conserved pathway that decreases protein synthesis.
source: Accumulation of misfolded proteins can activate the integrated stress response (ISR) (Harding et al., 2003), an evolutionary conserved pathway that decreases protein synthesis.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about the ISR pathway.

claim: The ISR may have a causative role in age-related cognitive decline.
source: In this way, the ISR may have a causative role in age-related cognitive decline.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that the authors test in the manuscript.

claim: ISRIB rescued traumatic brain injury-induced behavioral and cognitive deficits.
source: We previously discovered that interference with the drug-like small-molecule inhibitor (integrated stress response inhibitor, or ISRIB) rescued traumatic brain injury-induced behavioral and cognitive deficits (Chou et al., 2017; Krukowski et al., 2020; Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020), suggesting that this pharmacological tool may be useful in testing this notion.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: In old animals there is an increase in neuronal hyperpolarization after spiking activity (afterhyperpolarization, or AHP) that decreases intrinsic neuronal excitability and correlates with memory deficits.
source: Specifically, in old animals there is an increase in neuronal hyperpolarization after spiking activity ('afterhyperpolarization', or AHP) that decreases intrinsic neuronal excitability and correlates with memory deficits (Disterhoft and Oh, 2007; McKiernan and Marrone, 2017; Oh et al., 2010; Rizzo et al., 2014; Kaczorowski and Disterhoft, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Aging manifests itself with synaptic excitability changes in the hippocampus that correlate with a reduction in dendritic spines.
source: Aging also manifests itself with synaptic excitability changes in the hippocampus that correlate with a reduction in the bulbous membrane projections that form the postsynaptic specializations of excitatory synapses, termed dendritic spines (von Bohlen und Halbach et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Morphological changes in dendritic spine density are critical for spatial learning and memory.
source: Morphological changes in dendritic spine density are critical for spatial learning and memory (Bloss et al., 2011; Yasumatsu et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ISR activation can modify immune responses via alterations in cytokine production.
source: In addition to neuronal changes, ISR activation can modify immune responses via alterations in cytokine production (Onat et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Maladaptive immune responses have been linked with cognitive decline in the old brain.
source: Indeed, maladaptive immune responses have been linked with cognitive decline in the old brain (Yousef et al., 2019; Villeda et al., 2011; Villeda et al., 2014; Baruch et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Type-I IFN responses can induce age-related phenotypes in rodents.
source: Type-I IFN responses can induce age-related phenotypes in rodents.
evidence: This is inferred from the preceding discussion of IFN-mediated cognitive changes.

claim: The adaptive immune system (T-cell infiltration into the old brain) can regulate neuronal function via IFN-γ production.
source: Furthermore, the adaptive immune system (T-cell infiltration into the old brain) can regulate neuronal function via IFN-γ production (Dulken et al., 2019), suggesting the possibility that age-induced maladaptive immune responses and the ISR are linked.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: ISRIB administration decreased age-associated ATF4 protein levels in mouse brain lysates when compared to vehicle-treated controls during ISRIB administration.
source: Using the same ISRIB treatment paradigm of daily injections on 3 consecutive days (Chou et al., 2017; Krukowski et al., 2020), we found decreased age-associated ATF4 protein levels in mouse brain lysates when compared to vehicle-treated controls during ISRIB administration (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ATF4 levels 18 days after cessation of ISRIB treatment showed persistent reduction in age-induced ATF4 protein levels that were indistinguishable from young mice.
source: ATF4 levels 18 days after cessation of ISRIB treatment showed persistent reduction in age-induced ATF4 protein levels that were indistinguishable from young mice (Figure 1A,B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Four known kinases can phosphorylate Ser51 in the α-subunit of eIF2α to activate the ISR: HRI, PKR, PERK and GCN2.
source: Four known kinases can phosphorylate Ser51 in its α-subunit of (eIF2α) to activate the ISR (Wek, 2018): HRI (heme-regulated inhibitor), PKR (double-stranded RNA-dependent protein kinase), PERK (PKR-like ER kinase) and GCN2 (General amino acid control nonderepressible 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge about ISR kinases.

claim: Only three of the four ISR kinases are known to be expressed in the mammalian brain (PKR, PERK, GCN2).
source: Only three of these kinases are known to be expressed in the mammalian brain (PKR, PERK, GCN2).
evidence: This represents established knowledge about kinase expression in the brain.

claim: A modest, but significant increase in activated GCN2 (p-GCN2) was found when comparing young and old brain lysates.
source: We found a modest, but significant increase in activated GCN2 (as indicated by its phosphorylated form p-GCN2) when comparing young and old brain lysates (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: When ISRIB was administered weeks prior, GCN2 activation returned to levels comparable to young brains.
source: Moreover, when ISRIB was administered weeks prior (Figure 1A), GCN2 activation returned to levels comparable to young brains (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Age and ISRIB did not impact phosphorylation status of PERK and PKR in total brain lysates.
source: Age and ISRIB did not impact phosphorylation status of PERK and PKR in total brain lysates (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: Brief ISRIB administration in the old brain has long-lasting effects on ISR activation.
source: Thus, brief ISRIB administration in the old brain has long-lasting effects on ISR activation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing persistent reduction in ATF4 levels 18 days after treatment.

claim: After 2 days of training, young animals averaged one error prior to successfully locating the escape platform in the radial arm water maze.
source: After 2 days of training, young animals averaged one error prior to successfully locating the escape platform, whereas old animals averaged three errors, indicating their reduced learning capacity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: After 2 days of training, old animals averaged three errors prior to successfully locating the escape platform in the radial arm water maze, indicating their reduced learning capacity.
source: After 2 days of training, young animals averaged one error prior to successfully locating the escape platform, whereas old animals averaged three errors, indicating their reduced learning capacity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: By the end of 2 days of training, ISRIB-treated old animals averaged two errors prior to finding the escape platform, whereas vehicle-treated old animals averaged three, denoting significant learning improvement in the mice that received ISRIB.
source: By the end of 2 days of training, ISRIB-treated old animals averaged two errors prior to finding the escape platform, whereas vehicle-treated old animals averaged three, denoting significant learning improvement in the mice that received ISRIB (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: No difference in learning performance was measured in young mice that received the identical ISRIB treatment paradigm.
source: No difference in learning performance was measured in young mice that received the identical treatment paradigm (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that ISRIB-induced learning improvement measured in this training regime is age-dependent.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ISRIB-induced learning improvement measured in this training regime is age-dependent.
source: No difference in learning performance was measured in young mice that received the identical treatment paradigm (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that ISRIB-induced learning improvement measured in this training regime is age-dependent.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that young mice did not show improvement with ISRIB treatment.

claim: Old animals that received Cmp-003 made significantly fewer errors prior to locating the escape platform than old animals that received vehicle injections.
source: Old animals that received Cmp-003 made significantly fewer errors prior to locating the escape platform than old animals that received vehicle injections, again indicating significant learning improvement.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Old mice treated with ISRIB 1 week before made significantly fewer errors compared to matched, vehicle-treated-old male mice in the spatial memory test.
source: Old mice treated with ISRIB 1 week before made significantly fewer errors compared to matched, vehicle-treated-old male (Figure 2B) and female (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The memory performance of old animals treated with ISRIB a week before was comparable to that of young mice.
source: Remarkably, the memory performance of old animals treated with ISRIB a week before was comparable to that of young mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Brief treatment with ISRIB rescues age-induced spatial learning and memory deficits.
source: These results demonstrate that brief treatment with ISRIB rescues age-induced spatial learning and memory deficits, cementing a causative role of the ISR on long-term memory dysfunction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data presented.

claim: The ISR has a causative role on long-term memory dysfunction.
source: These results demonstrate that brief treatment with ISRIB rescues age-induced spatial learning and memory deficits, cementing a causative role of the ISR on long-term memory dysfunction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that ISR inhibition reverses memory deficits.

claim: Old mice display significant impairments in the delayed-matching-to-place paradigm when compared to young mice.
source: Previous work has demonstrated that old mice display significant impairments when compared to young mice (Yousef et al., 2019; Castellano et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Old mice that received ISRIB treatment 18 days earlier displayed significant improvement over the 4-day testing period in the delayed-matching-to-place paradigm.
source: Old mice that received ISRIB treatment 18 days earlier displayed significant improvement over the 4-day testing period (Figure 2C; Day 20 vs. Day 23).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: By Day 23, ISRIB post-treatment animals were locating the escape tunnel on average 20 s faster than the matched-vehicle group.
source: By Day 23, post-treatment animals were locating the escape tunnel on average 20 s faster than the matched-vehicle group (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Old animals that received vehicle injections did not learn the delayed-matching-to-place task.
source: By contrast, old animals that received vehicle injections did not learn the task (Figure 2C; Day 20 vs. Day 23), as previously observed (Yousef et al., 2019; Castellano et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C and citations to previous literature.

claim: ISRIB administration increases cognitive performance in a behavioral paradigm measured weeks after administration.
source: These results demonstrate that ISRIB administration increases cognitive performance in a behavioral paradigm measured weeks after administration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the delayed-matching-to-place data.

claim: Old mice displayed a significantly increased AHP amplitude when compared to young mice.
source: In agreement with previous reports (Disterhoft and Oh, 2007; McKiernan and Marrone, 2017; Oh et al., 2010; Rizzo et al., 2014; Kaczorowski and Disterhoft, 2009), old mice displayed a significantly increased AHP amplitude when compared to young mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3B and citations to previous literature.

claim: ISRIB treatment reversed the age-induced increase in AHP amplitude, rendering the CA1 neuronal response in ISRIB-treated old mice indistinguishable from young mice.
source: ISRIB treatment reversed the age-induced increase in AHP amplitude, rendering the CA1 neuronal response in ISRIB-treated old mice indistinguishable from young mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: No significant differences were found in other action potential or passive membrane properties between groups.
source: We did not find significant differences in other action potential or passive membrane properties between groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both the frequency and amplitude of sEPSCs were indistinguishable between groups.
source: Both the frequency and amplitude of sEPSCs were indistinguishable between groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: ISRIB treatment in old animals restores neuronal function to levels comparable to young neurons by affecting intrinsic excitability and specifically reducing the AHP following high-frequency firing.
source: These data support that ISRIB treatment in old animals restores neuronal function to levels comparable to young neurons by affecting intrinsic excitability and specifically reducing the AHP following high-frequency firing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiology data.

claim: The hippocampus of old mice is characterized by a reduction in dendritic spine density that correlates with diminished cognitive output.
source: The hippocampus of old mice is characterized by a reduction in dendritic spine density that correlates with diminished cognitive output (von Bohlen und Halbach et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A significant reduction in dendritic spine density was measured in old when compared to young Thy1-YFP mice.
source: Similar to previous reports, we measured a significant reduction in dendritic spine density in old when compared to young Thy1-YFP mice (Figure 3E; von Bohlen und Halbach et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3E and citations to previous literature.

claim: ISRIB treatment significantly increased spine numbers when compared with age-matched vehicle-treated mice.
source: ISRIB treatment significantly increased spine numbers when compared with age-matched vehicle-treated mice (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ISRIB administration improves both neuron structure and function in old mice.
source: Taken together these data demonstrate that ISRIB administration improves both neuron structure and function in old mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiology and spine density data.

claim: Immune dysregulation in the brain increases with age.
source: Because it is known that immune dysregulation in the brain increases with age (Oliveira Pisco et al., 2020) and correlates with reduced cognitive performance in old animals (Yousef et al., 2019; Villeda et al., 2011; Villeda et al., 2014; Baruch et al., 2014), we next investigated immune parameters impacted by ISRIB administration in the old brain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Immune dysregulation in the brain correlates with reduced cognitive performance in old animals.
source: Because it is known that immune dysregulation in the brain increases with age (Oliveira Pisco et al., 2020) and correlates with reduced cognitive performance in old animals (Yousef et al., 2019; Villeda et al., 2011; Villeda et al., 2014; Baruch et al., 2014), we next investigated immune parameters impacted by ISRIB administration in the old brain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: No differences in astrocyte and microglia reactivity were observed between old and ISRIB-treated old animals.
source: In these analyses, we observed no differences between the old and ISRIB-treated old animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-G).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Age increased expression of IFN response pathway genes Rtp4, Ifit1, and Gbp10.
source: Indeed, we found that age increased expression of a number of IFN response pathway genes, Rtp4, Ifit1, and Gbp10 (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: ISRIB administration reduced expression of Rtp4, Ifit1, and Gbp10 to levels that became indistinguishable from young animals.
source: Importantly, ISRIB administration reduced expression of Rtp4, Ifit1, and Gbp10 to levels that became indistinguishable from young animals (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Other inflammatory markers (Ccl2, Il6) were increased with age but not affected by ISRIB treatment.
source: Other inflammatory makers were also increased with age (Ccl2, Il6) but not affected by ISRIB treatment, whereas Cd11b was increased upon ISRIB administration alone (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Table 1.

claim: Cd11b was increased upon ISRIB administration alone.
source: Other inflammatory makers were also increased with age (Ccl2, Il6) but not affected by ISRIB treatment, whereas Cd11b was increased upon ISRIB administration alone (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Table 1.

claim: A significant increase in T cell marker mRNA expression (Cd3) was observed in the hippocampus of old compared to young mice.
source: Similar to other reports (Dulken et al., 2019; Mrdjen et al., 2018), we observed a significant increase in T cell marker mRNA expression (Cd3) in the hippocampus of old compared to young mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4D and citations to previous literature.

claim: ISRIB treatment in the old mice reduced the expression of the T cell marker to a level comparable to that observed in young mice.
source: ISRIB treatment in the old mice reduced the expression of the T cell marker to a level comparable to that observed in young mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CD8+ T cell percentages were reduced in peripheral blood following ISRIB administration.
source: The ISRIB-induced reduction in T cell marker levels was not limited to the brain but extended to the peripheral blood of old animals, with CD8+ T cell percentages reduced following ISRIB administration (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: No changes in CD4+ T cell levels were observed following ISRIB administration.
source: By contrast, we observed no changes in CD4+ T cell levels (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: T cell marker mRNA expression in the brain positively correlated with cognitive performance: mice with lower T cell marker expression made fewer errors prior to locating the escape platform during memory testing on Day 2.
source: T cell marker mRNA expression in the brain positively correlated with cognitive performance: mice with lower T cell marker expression made fewer errors prior to locating the escape platform during memory testing on Day 2 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Significant positive correlations were observed when comparing memory performance on day 2 (errors) with the mRNA levels of multiple IFN response pathway genes (Ifit1, Rtp4, Gbp10, Gbp5, Oasl1) and additional inflammatory markers (Ccl2, Il6).
source: We also observed significant positive correlations when comparing memory performance on day 2 (errors) with the mRNA levels of multiple IFN response pathway genes (Ifit1, Rtp4, Gbp10, Gbp5, Oasl1) and additional inflammatory markers (Ccl2, Il6) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Increased inflammatory marker expression corresponds with poorer cognitive performance.
source: These data demonstrate that increased inflammatory marker expression correspond with poorer cognitive performance, even when we did not observed differences between the groups.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the correlation data.

claim: ISRIB treatment impacts a broad number of immune parameters both in the periphery and in the brain reducing the age-related inflammatory tone which strongly correlates with improved cognition.
source: These studies revealed that ISRIB treatment impacts a broad number of immune parameters both in the periphery and in the brain reducing the age-related inflammatory tone which strongly correlates with improved cognition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immune and behavioral data.

claim: No differences were detected in Gadd34 (Ppp1r15a), Pkr (Eif2ak2), Bdnf1, and Ophn1 mRNA levels with age or ISRIB treatment.
source: We did not detect differences in Gadd34 (Ppp1r15a), Pkr (Eif2ak2), Bdnf1, and Ophn1 mRNA levels with age or ISRIB treatment (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Table 1.

claim: A negative correlation was found between Ppp1r15a mRNA and cognitive performance: animals with less Ppp1r15a mRNA made more errors prior to locating the escape platform during memory testing.
source: Interestingly however, when analyzed as individual animals, we found a negative correlation between Ppp1r15a mRNA and cognitive performance: animals with less Ppp1r15a mRNA made more errors prior to locating the escape platform during memory testing (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: GADD34 is the regulatory subunit of one of the two eIF2α phosphatases and acts in a feedback loop as a downstream target of ATF4.
source: GADD34, the regulatory subunit of one of the two eIF2α phosphatases, acts in a feedback loop as a downstream target of ATF4 (Brush et al., 2003; Connor et al., 2001; Novoa et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and represents established knowledge.

claim: Induction of GADD34 leads to decreased phosphorylation of eIF2 which counteracts ISR activation.
source: Induction of GADD34 leads to decreased phosphorylation of eIF2 which counteracts ISR activation.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about the ISR feedback loop.

claim: ISRIB treatment reduced p-eIF2 levels in total brain lysates.
source: Indeed, ISRIB treatment reduced p-eIF2 levels in total brain lysates (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting that ISRIB may break a feedback loop thereby resetting age-related ISR activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: ISRIB may break a feedback loop thereby resetting age-related ISR activation.
source: Indeed, ISRIB treatment reduced p-eIF2 levels in total brain lysates (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting that ISRIB may break a feedback loop thereby resetting age-related ISR activation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed reduction in p-eIF2 levels.

claim: Temporary treatment with ISRIB causes a long lasting down-regulation of ATF4 (measured up to 20 days post-treatment).
source: Here, we provide evidence for a direct involvement of the ISR in age-related cognitive decline. Temporary treatment with ISRIB causes a long lasting down-regulation of ATF4 (measured up to 20 days post-treatment).
evidence: This is a summary of the findings from the ATF4 Western blot data.

claim: The 'ISR reset' leads to improvement in spatial, working, and episodic memory.
source: The 'ISR reset' leads to improvement in spatial, working, and episodic memory.
evidence: This is a summary of the behavioral findings.

claim: Broad-spectrum anatomical, cellular, and functional changes are caused by ISR activation in old animals.
source: Thus, we identify broad-spectrum anatomical, cellular, and functional changes caused by ISR activation in old animals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the multiple types of data presented.

claim: If these findings in mice translate into human physiology, they offer hope and a tangible strategy to sustain cognitive ability as we age.
source: If these findings in mice translate into human physiology, they offer hope and a tangible strategy to sustain cognitive ability as we age.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential translational implications of the findings.

claim: Alterations in proteostasis is a hallmark of aging.
source: Alterations in proteostasis, the process of protein synthesis, folding and degradation, is a hallmark of aging (López-Otín et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge.

claim: Accumulation of protein aggregate in the brain is a contributing factor to disease development and progression in several age-related neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
source: Accumulation of protein aggregate in the brain is a contributing factor to disease development and progression in several age-related neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease (Powers et al., 2009; Hetz et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The rate of protein synthesis reportedly declines with age in various regions of the brain.
source: The rate of protein synthesis reportedly also declines with age in various regions of the brain (Schimanski and Barnes, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Protein synthesis is critical for memory consolidation.
source: Protein synthesis is critical for memory consolidation and the ISR pathway is one of the major nodes for protein synthesis control.
evidence: This represents established knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: The ISR pathway is one of the major nodes for protein synthesis control.
source: Protein synthesis is critical for memory consolidation and the ISR pathway is one of the major nodes for protein synthesis control.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about the ISR.

claim: ISRIB rapidly enters the brain of old animals and interferes with ISR activation as measured by decreased phosphorylation of eIF2α and ATF4 levels.
source: ISRIB rapidly enters the brain of old animals and interferes with ISR activation as measured by decreased phosphorylation of eIF2α and ATF4 levels.
evidence: This is a summary of the Western blot findings.

claim: ISRIB acts downstream of phosphorylation of eIF2α.
source: ISRIB acts downstream of phosphorylation of eIF2α Sidrauski et al., 2013; therefore, the decrease in phosphorylation of eIF2α suggests a possible block in the feedback loop that keeps the ISR activated in the old brain; further investigation is needed to understand the exact mechanism.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge about ISRIB's mechanism of action.

claim: The decrease in phosphorylation of eIF2α suggests a possible block in the feedback loop that keeps the ISR activated in the old brain.
source: ISRIB acts downstream of phosphorylation of eIF2α Sidrauski et al., 2013; therefore, the decrease in phosphorylation of eIF2α suggests a possible block in the feedback loop that keeps the ISR activated in the old brain; further investigation is needed to understand the exact mechanism.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed decrease in p-eIF2α.

claim: Age increased activation of GCN2 (denoted by increased phosphorylation) which was attenuated by ISRIB administration.
source: Initial findings suggest this could be through modulation of the kinase GCN2. Here we found that age increased activation of GCN2 (denoted by increased phosphorylation) was attenuated by ISRIB administration.
evidence: This is a summary of the Western blot findings for p-GCN2.

claim: Even brief inhibition of the ISR allows the system to 'reset' and dampen the stress response in the old brain.
source: These data indicate that even brief inhibition of the ISR allows the system to 'reset' and dampen the stress response in the old brain.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the long-lasting effects of ISRIB on ISR markers.

claim: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) is an important pathway that cells employ to respond to environmental stress and balance between survival and death.
source: Along with the ISR, the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), is the other important pathway that cells employ to respond to environmental stress and balance between survival and death.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about mTOR signaling.

claim: Rapamycin targets mTOR and therefore inhibits mTOR-controlled mRNA translation.
source: Rapamycin, arguably the most studied and validated small molecule for lifespan expansion, targets mTOR and therefore inhibits mTOR-controlled mRNA translation.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about rapamycin's mechanism of action.

claim: Increased protein production due to mTOR (over)activation can in turn induce the ISR.
source: However, increased protein production due to mTOR (over)activation can in turn induce the ISR (Tenkerian et al., 2015; Cagnetta et al., 2019; Koromilas, 2019), which serves as a governor keeping protein synthesis in check.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both the ISR and mTOR converge at the level of mRNA translation and both inhibit the translation of the same set of proteins.
source: Interestingly, despite these two pathways regulating distinct stress responses to translational regulation, it was recently reported that both the ISR and mTOR converge at the level of mRNA translation and both inhibit the translation of the same set of proteins (Klann et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to recent literature.

claim: The complex interplay between mTOR signaling and the ISR could potentially explain how pharmacological treatment with seemingly opposing strategies could both be beneficial.
source: This complex interplay between mTOR signaling and the ISR could potentially explain how pharmacological treatment with seemingly opposing strategies could both be beneficial.
evidence: This is speculation about the relationship between mTOR and ISR pathways.

claim: Brief ISRIB treatment improved performance in two different behavioral paradigms (radial arm water maze and the delayed matching to place) previously shown to capture age-related cognitive decline.
source: Importantly, brief ISRIB treatment improved performance in two different behavioral paradigms (radial arm water maze and the delayed matching to place) previously shown to capture age-related cognitive decline (Yousef et al., 2019; Castellano et al., 2017; Villeda et al., 2014; Deczkowska et al., 2017; Horowitz et al., 2020; Smith et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a summary of the behavioral findings with citations to previous literature validating the paradigms.

claim: These behavioral paradigms model different aspects of cognitive loss observed during aging in rodents: spatial, working, and episodic memory.
source: These behavioral paradigms model different aspects of cognitive loss observed during aging in rodents: spatial, working, and episodic memory (Alamed et al., 2006; Feng et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ISR inhibition can reverse a broad spectrum of cognitive decline.
source: Therefore, our results suggest that ISR inhibition can reverse a broad spectrum of cognitive decline.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the multiple behavioral improvements observed.

claim: Spatial learning reversal occurred during ISRIB treatment while the effects on memory were measured weeks after administration.
source: Notably, spatial learning reversal occurred during ISRIB treatment while the effects on memory were measured weeks after administration and demonstrate the long lasting effects of ISRIB even in the aging brain.
evidence: This is a summary of the temporal aspects of the behavioral findings.

claim: Most of the previous studies on age-related cognitive decline were performed exclusively in male rodents.
source: Most of the previous studies were performed exclusively in male rodents (Villeda et al., 2014; Deczkowska et al., 2017; Horowitz et al., 2020; Smith et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sex-dimorphic cognitive decline has been reported with age in humans and rodents.
source: Sex-dimorphic cognitive decline has been reported with age in humans (Casaletto et al., 2019; Casaletto et al., 2020; Jack et al., 2015) and rodents (Davis et al., 2019; Davis et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cognitive reversal with ISRIB administration was identified in both male and female mice.
source: In the current study, we identified cognitive reversal with ISRIB administration in both male and female mice; taking the critical first steps towards studying sex-dimorphic age responses in the ISR.
evidence: This is a summary of the behavioral findings in both sexes.

claim: ISRIB-mediated neuronal and immune correlates were only validated in male mice.
source: However, we only validated ISRIB-mediated neuronal and immune correlates in male mice.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation in the study design.

claim: An increase of AHP is associated with aging and impaired learning in young adult rodents.
source: An increase of AHP is associated with aging (Kaczorowski and Disterhoft, 2009; Gant et al., 2006) and impaired learning in young adult rodents (Oh et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Changes in dendritic spine density or structural reorganization of spines are important for synaptic function and cognitive processes such as learning and memory.
source: Changes in dendritic spine density or structural reorganization of spines are important for synaptic function (Ultanir et al., 2007) and cognitive processes such as learning and memory (Bloss et al., 2011; Yasumatsu et al., 2008; Frank et al., 2018; Lu and Zuo, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the aging brain, there is a reduction in hippocampal spine density that has been suggested to be responsible for the poor memory functions.
source: In the aging brain, there is a reduction in hippocampal spine density that has been suggested to be responsible for the poor memory functions (Cabral-Miranda et al., 2020; von Bohlen und Halbach et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Age-related molecular processes linked to spine loss include disruption in local protein synthesis.
source: A number of age-related molecular processes have been linked to spine loss including disruption in local protein synthesis (Tolino et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Type I IFN responses are increased with age.
source: The importance of this molecule in age-related decline has been demonstrated: Type I IFN responses are increased with age, IFN-β expression in the brain is associated with cognitive decline, and injection of IFN-β expressing viral vectors into an adult mouse can induce an old phenotype (Baruch et al., 2014; Deczkowska et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: IFN-β expression in the brain is associated with cognitive decline.
source: The importance of this molecule in age-related decline has been demonstrated: Type I IFN responses are increased with age, IFN-β expression in the brain is associated with cognitive decline, and injection of IFN-β expressing viral vectors into an adult mouse can induce an old phenotype (Baruch et al., 2014; Deczkowska et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Injection of IFN-β expressing viral vectors into an adult mouse can induce an old phenotype.
source: The importance of this molecule in age-related decline has been demonstrated: Type I IFN responses are increased with age, IFN-β expression in the brain is associated with cognitive decline, and injection of IFN-β expressing viral vectors into an adult mouse can induce an old phenotype (Baruch et al., 2014; Deczkowska et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ISRIB administration reversed age-induced type I IFN responses in the hippocampus.
source: Here, we found that ISRIB administration reversed age-induced type I IFN responses in the hippocampus suggesting that ISR activation plays a role in this pathway.
evidence: This is a summary of the qPCR findings for IFN-related genes.

claim: ISR activation plays a role in the type I IFN response pathway.
source: Here, we found that ISRIB administration reversed age-induced type I IFN responses in the hippocampus suggesting that ISR activation plays a role in this pathway.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that ISR inhibition reduces IFN responses.

claim: It is unclear if ISRIB's effect on IFN responses is via a direct or indirect effect on inflammatory cells.
source: However, it is still unclear if this is via a direct or indirect effect on inflammatory cells.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of uncertainty about the mechanism.

claim: Persistent T cell infiltration in the brain following viral infection leads to synapse loss.
source: Two recent reports found that persistent T cell infiltration in the brain following viral infection leads to synapse loss (Garber et al., 2019; Di Liberto et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: IFN-γ produced by T-cells mediates synapse loss.
source: Investigators identified that IFN-γ produced by T-cells-mediated synapse loss (Garber et al., 2019; Di Liberto et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: ISRIB treatment impacted T cell levels both in the brain and periphery.
source: Here, we find that ISRIB treatment impacted T cell levels both in the brain and periphery.
evidence: This is a summary of the qPCR and flow cytometry findings.

claim: The changes in T cells and IFN responses directly correlated with cognitive performance and were restored by ISRIB to the levels observed in young animals.
source: The changes in T cells and IFN responses directly correlated with cognitive performance and, again, were restored by ISRIB to the levels observed in young animals.
evidence: This is a summary of the correlation analysis and treatment effects.

claim: Whether ISRIB reverses cognitive decline by directly modulating one of the measured processes (neuronal intrinsic excitability, dendritic spine number, IFN response, or T cell numbers) or by impacting a number of them remains to be determined.
source: Whether ISRIB reverses cognitive decline by directly modulating one of the measured processes (neuronal intrinsic excitability, dendritic spine number, IFN response, or T cell numbers) or by impacting a number of them remains to be determined.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of uncertainty about the causal mechanisms.

claim: Pharmacological attenuation of the ISR can alleviate age-related neuronal and immune changes potentially resetting age-induced cognitive decline.
source: Here, we demonstrate that pharmacological attenuation of the ISR can alleviate age-related neuronal and immune changes potentially resetting age-induced cognitive decline.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, drawing on all the presented data.

claim: Old animals started experimentation at approximately 19 months of age and young animals at 3–6 months of age.
source: Old animals started experimentation at ∼19 months of age and young animals 3–6 months of age.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: ISRIB stock solution was at 0.1 mg/ml and injections were at 2.5 mg/kg.
source: Stock ISRIB solution was at 0.1 mg/ml and injections were at 2.5 mg/kg.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: ATF4 is a well-studied ISR-upregulated target protein.
source: One well-studied ISR-upregulated target protein is ATF4 (activating transcription factor 4) (Chen et al., 2003; Pasini et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and represents established knowledge.

claim: ISRIB administration reversed mild head trauma-induced elevation in ATF4 protein.
source: We recently showed ISRIB administration reversed mild head trauma-induced elevation in ATF4 protein (Krukowski et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.
